items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: The only one that I got to really like was Baby James. This cat had a nice sound and he played those things of Louis nice, you know.

ctx.x: He was offering him a job, because the money was a meal-ticket type of thing with us, you know, and me being the leader, maybe I might get five dollars extra a week or something like that. Cats just... It was very simple. You'd meet the cat somewhere: "Hey, come over here. You'll get this. They ain't doin' nothin'..."

Then we went from there to St. Louis, and I had a trunk full of clothes. And when I got to St. Louis and the trunk got there, wasn't a stitch in that trunk. Nothing. We stayed around there at that hotel, the Grand Central or Grand Something... And them trumpet players used to come in every Sunday on me -- Dewey Jackson, Baby James, and some big cat, I never did know his name, that looked like Louis Armstrong, a big fat cat... And they all played "Butter And Egg Man"...all of those things that Louis used to play…
